title: Neonatal jaundice (India, IAP)
subject: paediatrics
setting: Labour room, postnatal ward, SNCU, NICU, newborn follow-up clinic
summary: Examine every newborn for jaundice at least every 12 hours for the first 3 to 5 days and before discharge. Jaundice in the first 24 hours, yellow palms and soles or signs of encephalopathy are serious: start intensive phototherapy, measure TSB, plot it on hour-specific charts, and refer early for exchange transfusion when indicated.

sections.title: Recognise serious jaundice
items: Physiological jaundice appears after 24 hours, falls after day 5 to 6, is gone by 14 days and seldom exceeds 15 mg/dL.

Serious jaundice: visible in the first 24 hours; yellow palms and soles at any time; TSB above the 95th centile (or at the phototherapy line) on hour-specific AAP or NICE charts; or signs of acute bilirubin encephalopathy.
Acute bilirubin encephalopathy: poor suck or feeding, lethargy, hypotonia or hypertonia, high-pitched cry, irritability, arching, retrocollis, opisthotonus, fever or seizures.

Risk factors needing closer watch: gestation below 38 weeks, previous sibling treated for jaundice, ABO or Rh incompatibility (mother Rh-negative or group O), G6PD deficiency, cephalohaematoma, breastfeeding not established or weight loss above 3% a day or 10% in total, predischarge TcB or TSB in the high or high-intermediate risk zone (TcB above 13 mg/dL).

sections.title: Assess and measure
items: Examine the naked baby in bright natural or white fluorescent light, pressing the skin to blanch it, at least every 12 hours during the first 3 to 5 days. Kramer zones (approximate TSB): face and neck 4 to 6 mg/dL; chest and upper abdomen 8 to 10; lower abdomen and thighs 12 to 14; arms and legs 15 to 18; palms and soles above 15 to 20 mg/dL.

Measure TSB (or TcB) if jaundice appears in the first 24 hours, if visual or TcB estimate beyond 24 hours is above 12 to 14 mg/dL or near the phototherapy cut-off, or if unsure. Plot against age in hours.

Collect cord or early venous blood for blood group and direct Coombs test if the mother is Rh-negative or group O. Suspected haemolysis: CBC, reticulocyte count, peripheral smear and DCT. Screen for G6PD deficiency in high-prevalence areas.

Repeat TSB according to cause and severity: every 6 to 8 hours in the first 24 to 48 hours of haemolytic jaundice, every 12 to 24 hours for non-haemolytic jaundice. Do not rely on visual assessment or TcB during phototherapy.

Prolonged jaundice (beyond 2 weeks in term, 3 weeks in preterm): total and direct bilirubin, thyroid function, urine reducing substances and culture; ask about pale stools and dark urine and arrange abdominal ultrasound to exclude biliary atresia.

sections.title: Phototherapy
items: Start intensive phototherapy at once (after sending TSB) for serious jaundice, and whenever TSB is at or above the phototherapy cut-off for age in hours and risk on AAP or NICE charts.
Use blue light of adequate irradiance (above 30 microW/cm2 per nm), usually from LED or CFL units, and check the irradiance every 6 months.
Keep the baby naked except a small nappy and eye covers, place the lights as close as possible without overheating, expose the maximum skin area, and monitor temperature.
Continue frequent breastfeeding; phototherapy may be interrupted briefly for feeds and procedures. Ensure adequate stool and urine output.
Stop phototherapy when TSB falls 2 to 3 mg/dL below the phototherapy line (the ICMR STW uses below 13 to 14 mg/dL or 2 mg/dL below the cut-off).

sections.title: Exchange transfusion and referral
items: Immediate exchange blood transfusion for signs of acute bilirubin encephalopathy or TSB above the age- and risk-specific exchange cut-off; start intensive phototherapy while preparing.

Refer early to a centre able to do exchange transfusion if TSB is not responding to intensive phototherapy, or if jaundice appeared in the first 24 hours, the baby is preterm or sick (sepsis), or a previous sibling needed exchange: these babies are at risk at lower levels.
Exchange volume is twice the estimated blood volume (blood volume 80 to 100 mL/kg). Blood must be cross-matched with the mother's blood; send the mother's sample if she cannot accompany the baby.

Rh isoimmunisation: O-negative packed cells in AB plasma, O-negative whole blood, or Rh-negative blood of the baby's ABO group. ABO isoimmunisation: group O (Rh-compatible) packed cells in AB plasma or group O whole blood. Otherwise use the baby's group.

sections.title: Discharge and follow-up
items: Do a predischarge risk assessment on an hour-specific nomogram; a value in the high-risk zone needs re-evaluation within 24 hours.

Review all babies within 48 hours of discharge (within 24 hours if at risk); ICMR advises follow-up 48 to 72 hours after discharge for babies discharged before 72 hours. Check for jaundice, feeding problems, weight loss, stool and urine output.
After significant hyperbilirubinaemia, follow neurodevelopment with screening tools until school age, including early language milestones.
After encephalopathy or exchange transfusion, test hearing with brainstem evoked response audiometry before 6 months of age.

sections.title: Prevention
items: Early and frequent breastfeeding, or early mother's own milk in the NICU; reinforce breastfeeding at discharge.
Know the mother's blood group, and test the baby's group and DCT (cord or early venous sample) when the mother is group O or Rh-negative.
Avoid naphthalene balls (haemolysis in G6PD deficiency).

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Using sunlight to treat jaundice.
Giving phenobarbitone to treat hyperbilirubinaemia.
Stopping breastfeeding.
Judging jaundice under poor hospital lighting, or by eye while the baby is under phototherapy.
Missing pale stools of biliary atresia in prolonged jaundice.

drugs.name: Intensive phototherapy
drugs.dose: Blue light, irradiance above 30 microW/cm2 per nm, maximum skin exposure
drugs.notes: Stop when TSB is 2 to 3 mg/dL below the treatment line.

drugs.name: Exchange blood transfusion
drugs.dose: Twice the estimated blood volume (2 x 80 to 100 mL/kg)
drugs.notes: Cross-matched with maternal blood; group choice depends on Rh or ABO isoimmunisation.
